newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: ASEAN says 1997 regional economic growth at 7-8 pc.
newsitem.headline: ASEAN says 1997 regional economic growth at 7-8 pc.

text.p: Economic growth in the nine-member Association of South East Asian Nations (ASEAN) is forecast to reach seven to eight percent in 1997, the group's Secretary-General Ajit Singh said on Monday.
"Economic growth in ASEAN is forecast to reach between seven and eight percent in 1997 bolstered by investment, exports and consumer spending," Singh said in a report on ASEAN economic cooperation.

The report was presented at an annual meeting of the Association of of South East Asian Nations -- Brunei, Burma, Indonesia, Laos, Malaysia, the Philippines, Singapore, Thailand and Vietnam -- and their "dialogue partners" comprising major Western and Asian powers.
Inflation in the nine economies was expected to ease to 4.6 percent this year from 4.8 percent in 1996, the report said.

With the admission of Laos and Burma, ASEAN now has a combined population of 481.2 million people, a total gross domestic product (GDP) of $632.5 billion, per capita GDP of $1,314 and combined exports of about $339.2 billion, Singh said.
ASEAN is the major investor in its two new members, accounting for 52 percent of total investment in Laos and 44 percent in Burma.
This year marks the halfway point in the implementation of an ASEAN Free Trade Area by 2003, under which tariffs are to be reduced to between zero and five percent.

As of May 31, member countries have included 42,253 tariff lines -- or 91 percent of all tariff lines in the region -- in the scheme so far. "Average tariff rates for products in the Inclusion List have now fallen to 6.38 percent from 12.7 percent in 1993," Singh said.
With the participation of Burma and Laos -- who have until 2008 to conform to the low-tariff regime -- the Inclusion List will increase to 45,119 tariff lines, or 81 percent of the total, he said.
Intra-ASEAN trade in the first three-quarters of 1996 reached $56.07 billion, 10 percent higher than the same period of the previous year, the report said.
ASEAN's total trade with the world is an estimated $550 billion.
